channel.title: Sample: Technology
channel.description: Made-up sample stories for trying out the news reader. None of these companies or events are real.

item.title: Northwind Robotics opens its first fully automated warehouse in Leeds
item.description: The fictional robotics firm says its new site can sort 40,000 parcels an hour with a team of twelve people overseeing the machines.

item.title: Kestrel Labs releases an open-source tool for cleaning messy spreadsheets
item.description: The free tool spots duplicate rows, mixed date formats and stray spaces, and explains each fix in plain English.

item.title: Why every data team is talking about small, fast databases
item.description: Engineers at three made-up start-ups explain how they replaced heavyweight systems with simpler tools that run on a laptop.

item.title: Lumen Mobile's new phone promises a week of battery life
item.description: Reviewers of the imaginary handset say the claim holds up, as long as you don't use the camera much.

item.title: A beginner's guide to reading RSS feeds in Python
item.description: RSS has been around since the late 1990s and is still one of the simplest ways to follow many websites at once.

item.title: Copperline Cloud cuts prices for students learning to code
item.description: The fictional provider now offers free accounts to anyone enrolled on a recognised coding course.
